description:
Wave-3 duplicate-check triage (2026-03-12, post wave-2) identifies 7
consolidation-worthy groups in the SQL platform adapter layer. These are
parallel implementations across platform adapters that can share a base
implementation via utilities, mixins, or extraction to existing shared modules.

Targets (report rank -> dup lines):

G11 (48 dup lines): apply_table_tunings in firebolt.py:1227, lakesail.py:604,
    presto.py:1051. 3 copies with 97% identical logic: check has_any_tuning() ->
    get partitioning columns -> sort by order -> log. Only ImportError handling
    and log messages differ across platforms.

G12 (47 dup lines): _build_lakesail_config and _build_synapse_config in
    azure_synapse.py:1341 and lakesail.py:686. Identical Azure-compatible
    config builder pattern. Both construct connection configs from the same
    parameter set with platform-specific defaults.

G16 (46 dup lines): create_schema in presto.py:635 and trino.py:647.
    Byte-for-byte identical schema creation logic. Textbook extension of
    the existing presto_trino_utils.py from wave-2 (which already holds
    the shared _validate_catalog_exists utility).

G18+G28 (88 dup lines combined): _execute_statement in
    fabric_spark_adapter.py:419 and synapse_spark_adapter.py:402, plus
    _wait_for_statement in fabric_spark_adapter.py:465 and
    synapse_spark_adapter.py:448. Two pairs of identical methods in the
    Azure Spark adapter family. Both adapters use the same Livy-based
    statement execution and polling pattern.

G23 (44 dup lines): get_query_plan across 5 platforms: athena.py:1193,
    azure_synapse.py:1200, firebolt.py:1124, presto.py:958, trino.py:956.
    Verbatim identical: cursor -> EXPLAIN query -> fetchall -> join rows.
    No platform-specific differences whatsoever.

G24 (44 dup lines): _parse_gcs_url and _parse_s3_url in
    clickhouse_cloud.py:880/:904 and firebolt.py:999. Cloud storage URL
    parsing utilities duplicated across platforms. These extract bucket
    and path from gs:// and s3:// URLs using the same regex/split logic.

G26 (44 dup lines): _extract_table_name across 6 platforms:
    firebolt.py:1063, lakesail.py:504, presto.py:913, redshift.py:1692,
    spark.py:539, trino.py:913. Identical SQL table name extraction from
    CREATE TABLE with shared regex pattern (IF NOT EXISTS variant) and
    try/except/pass structure. 4 additional platforms (azure_synapse:1102,
    athena:1176, fabric_warehouse:1223, questdb:437) have platform-specific
    regex variants (bracket-quoting, EXTERNAL TABLE, schema-qualified names,
    quote-handling) and are excluded from this consolidation.

anti_patterns.dont: create a deep inheritance hierarchy for platform adapters
anti_patterns.instead: use standalone utility functions or thin mixins
anti_patterns.why: platform adapters are frequently added/modified by contributors unfamiliar with the class hierarchy; utility functions are easier to discover and compose than deep class chains

anti_patterns.dont: merge Fabric and Synapse Spark adapters
anti_patterns.why: Fabric has workspace-scoped Lakehouse/Warehouse semantics that Synapse lacks; only the Livy execution layer is shared

anti_patterns.dont: merge Presto and Trino into a single adapter class
anti_patterns.instead: only share specific utilities via presto_trino_utils.py
anti_patterns.why: they diverge on features (Trino adds fault-tolerant execution, Presto has different auth) and a merged class would accumulate platform-specific branches

anti_patterns.instead: only consolidate the specific 3 platforms (firebolt, lakesail, presto) that are 97% identical
anti_patterns.why: other platforms (BigQuery, Snowflake, DuckDB) use radically different tuning mechanisms (clustering, micro-partitions, pragmas) and a universal abstraction would be leaky

anti_patterns.instead: keep explicit parameters matching the current signatures
anti_patterns.why: explicit parameters preserve type safety and IDE navigability across the 2 consuming adapters

preserves.behavior: Azure Spark statement execution and polling semantics unchanged
Azure config builders produce identical connection parameters
Cloud URL parsing returns identical (bucket, path) tuples
_extract_table_name returns identical table name strings from DDL
apply_table_tunings behavior identical per platform (including ImportError handling)
create_schema DDL output byte-for-byte identical for Presto and Trino
get_query_plan output format identical (newline-joined plan rows)
